div.head: VII Atr 2
div.ab: Et instituimus, ut omnis Christianus, qui ętatem habet, ieiunet tribus diebus in pane et aqua et herbis crudis.
Et instituimus, ut omnis Christianus qui aetatem habet ieiunet tribus diebus in pane et aqua et herbis crudis.
Et instituimus, ut omnis Christianus, qui aetatem habet, ieiunet tribus diebus in pane et aqua et herbis crudis.
Und wir bestimmen, dass jeder Christ, der das Alter [des Erwachsenen] hat, drei Tage bei Brot und Wasser und rohen Kräutern faste.
And we decree that every Christian who is of [adult] age fast for three days on bread and water and raw herbs.
And we have decreed that every adult Christian shall fast on bread and water and raw herbs for three days.
And we have decreed that every Christian who has reached adulthood is to fast for three days upon bread, water, and raw herbs.
div.note: Br adds ‘ante festum s. Michaelis’ (from 2.3a?). Liebermann compares VIIa Atr 1.
herbis crudis: bis crudis Br M; erudis Hk; Br adds ante festum sancti Michaelis

note.seg: bis crudis MBr; erudis Hk; ante festum s. Michaelis fügt Br zu [aus 2, 3a?]
bis crudis MBr; erudis Hk; Br adds ante festum s. Michaelis [from 2, 3a?]
Genannt u. 2, 3 und in logischerer Anordnung hier in Br, schon zu Anfang VIIa 1. Da die Homileten für die Zukunft schreiben, lassen sie den Termin fort
Named below 2, 3 and, in a more logical arrangement, here in Br; already at the beginning in VIIa 1. Since the homilists are writing for the future, they leave out the date
berenan hlafe, to sealte, grenan wyrtan (Gerstenbrot, Salz, grünen Kräutern) Hom. 173 [to ofete (in Frucht und Gemüse) Nachtrag]. All dies fehlt VIIa
berenan hlafe, to sealte, grenan wyrtan (barley bread, salt, green herbs) Hom. 173 [to ofete (on fruit and vegetables) a later addition]. All this is missing in VIIa
Cf. II As. 23; Wulfstan, p. 173, which reads: to berenan hlafe, to sealte and to grenan wyrtan.
